exposure: obstetric factors (history of cesarean section, vaginal delivery, nulliparity, multiparity, grand multiparity)
age (young adults, older age, advanced age)
ethnic factors (Karanki ethnicity, Awa ethnicity, white women)
cohort: The study included 2039 women with urinary incontinence recruited across the provinces of Imbabura, Carchi, and Esmeraldas in Ecuador.
finding: Urinary incontinence in women is statistically associated with various obstetric, age-related, and ethnic risk factors.
mod_finding: Stress and mixed urinary incontinence were significantly associated with a history of cesarean section, while urge urinary incontinence was associated with vaginal delivery.
